note: Prompts from model-check-skill-notes/14-skill-building-plan.md §8.2 (E1–E6). Each eval has 'assertions' (plan §8.2 as amended; 'expectations' is the key of grading.json only). Every assertion has a 'text' for the human reader and a 'check' a grader applies without judgement: regex / not_regex / regex_order run over the answer text (Python re, flags given in the pattern); petri_json_valid looks for a JSON file in the run's outputs directory that the engine's Petri frontend accepts and, when 'equivalent_to' is set, that has the same places, initial marking, transitions and arcs as that fixture; json_field reads a value from a JSON file in the outputs directory. 'runnable_from' names the build step from which the engine can execute the eval (G0: Petri JSON via the mcd CLI; G1: Promela; G4: ltl/progress/weak fairness; G5: ctl). An eval may carry 'variant_of' (it varies another eval's question on a different model) and 'dir' (the workspace directory name, when it is not 'eval-<id>-<name>'). Corpus fixtures are referenced by path and SHA-256 in evals/fixtures/README.md; evals/fixtures/petrinet1.json is the skill's own encoding, not a corpus copy. Grader: model-check-plugin/evals-workspace/grader.py. Since the review of 2026-09-29 (steps/review-astra-skill.md §D, steps/review-sol-reconciliation.md §5), an assertion that the engine was invoked is a `engine_report` check and not a regex over the prose: it looks for a file under the run's outputs directory that the engine itself wrote (engine.name = mcd, engine.report_schema = mcd-report/*) and, when given, for the property id, status and evidence in it. A run therefore has to save each mc_check report into its outputs directory; an answer that only talks about having run the engine now fails those assertions, which is the point. An eval may carry 'first_measured_in': the workspace iteration at which it entered the set. Earlier iterations are historical snapshots and are not expected to contain it; the latest iteration is expected to contain every eval the engine can run, which is what keeps a new eval from staying unmeasured.

evals.name: mutex-invariant-violated
evals.prompt: Два процесса не должны одновременно попадать в критическую секцию. Проверь эту модель: Promela - examples/CH2/mutex_flaw.pml
evals.expected_output: Invariant violated; status `violated`, evidence `exhaustive`; counterexample decoded through labels L1–L4 with both users at L7; cause class: system defect; the report's engine/inputs sections (manifest) attached; no forbidden phrasing; the engine's report JSON saved into the run's outputs directory.

assertions.text: The mutual-exclusion property is reported with status violated
The evidence level exhaustive is stated
The counterexample is decoded through the model's labels L1–L4
The counterexample shows both users at label L7 (the critical section)
The cause is classified as a system (algorithm) defect
The engine was invoked (CLI or MCP) and its report is among the run's outputs: property `assert` violated with evidence exhaustive
The engine version and input hash (manifest) are quoted
No forbidden phrasing (no errors / proved / system is correct) (a line that rejects the word does not count)

check.pattern: (?im)^(?![^\n]*(не\s|нельзя|не говор|not |never |avoid|do not|don't|forbidden|запрещ))[^\n]*(\bno errors\b|ошибок нет|\bproved\b|\bproven\b|доказано|system is correct|система корректна)

evals.name: alternating-bit-liveness-fairness
evals.prompt: Докажи, что alternating bit доставляет каждое сообщение. Модель: Promela - examples/CH3/alternatingbit.pml
evals.expected_output: Delivery is formalised as an LTL formula over the model and checked; the fairness question is raised (as a question or as an explicitly labelled assumption) before the liveness run; the result is `verified` with evidence `exhaustive`, and the answer says the verdict does not depend on the fairness setting because sender and receiver alternate in lock-step. The claim is limited to this model: it has no message loss, no retransmission and no timeout, so nothing is said about the alternating-bit protocol's behaviour on a lossy channel. The word "proved" is not used for the model result; the engine's report JSON saved into the run's outputs directory.

The delivery (liveness) property is reported verified
The evidence level exhaustive is stated
The formula that was actually checked is shown, in LTL syntax
The answer says the verdict does not depend on the fairness setting (the model is lock-step)

evals.name: telephone-busy-liveness
evals.prompt: Телефон не может зависнуть в состоянии Busy? Модель коммутатора: Promela - examples/CH14/version1
evals.expected_output: Requirement classified as liveness. Two legitimate routes, and the answer has to pick one and say why: (a) CTL, which accepts control-label atoms — `AG EF switch@Idle` (or the `:pid` form) runs as written on the model; (b) LTL, whose parser rejects `@`, so it needs a `progress` label placed in a rewrite (declared as a change to the model) and the `progress` property the Promela frontend then adds by itself. Fairness raised before the run for the LTL route; status and evidence from the vocabulary; the engine's report saved into the run's outputs directory.

assertions.text: The requirement is classified as a liveness property
The requirement is formalised either as a progress label / LTL eventually, or as a CTL formula over the control label
The formula refers to the model's labels or states (Busy), not to printf output
Fairness is raised before the result
A status from the vocabulary is given
An evidence level is given
The route is named correctly: either the `progress` property the frontend adds from progress labels, or the CTL formula with a control-label atom
If the route needs a change to the model (a progress label or a new variable), that change is declared; a CTL answer over the existing label needs no such change and says so

check.pattern: (?i)((добав\w+|постав\w+|размест\w+|внёс|внес\w+|перепис\w+|измен\w+|add\w*|plac\w*|insert\w*|chang\w*)[^\n]{0,80}(progress|метк|label|переменн)|(без изменен|не меня\w+ модел|without (a )?chang|no change to the model|модель не меня))

assertions.text: No forbidden phrasing (naming the word in order to deny it does not count)
The engine was invoked and its report is among the run's outputs, carrying the property of the route taken (progress, or ctl for the control-label route)

evals.name: ir-from-words
evals.prompt: Готовой модели нет, система описана только словами: два клиента делят один сервер. Клиент посылает запрос, ждёт разрешения, работает, затем сообщает об освобождении. Сервер выдаёт разрешение одному клиенту за раз и принимает следующий запрос только после освобождения. Вопросы: могут ли два клиента работать одновременно и может ли система зависнуть?
evals.expected_output: The model is built by the agent from the words alone (no model is given). The route is the one the skill prescribes: write it in the Promela subset first — direct IR authoring is experimental (plan 14 §12, A7) — then mc_parse, then mc_check with the two questions: the mutual-exclusion assert and deadlock. Both come back `verified` / `exhaustive` on a correct model (the hand-written reference `evals/fixtures/handshake.pml` gives deadlock verified and assert verified, exhaustive, 12 states). The answer must say that a verdict on a self-built model carries one more assumption than a verdict on a model the user gave — that the model says what the words said — and name the modelling decisions that the words did not fix (rendezvous or buffered channels, whether the server may reorder, what "works" means). The engine's report JSON saved into the run's outputs directory.
evals.note: This is the eval plan 14 §12 promises for assumption A7 («агент способен сам порождать модель для системы, заданной словами») and which G5 did not run; added by the review-fix pass of 2026-09-29 (steps/review-sol-reconciliation.md §1, row A2). The fixture is the comparison model, not an input: the agent never sees it. The comparison with the hand-written reference is by **verdict**, not by structure: the reference `evals/fixtures/handshake.pml` gives deadlock verified/exhaustive and its mutual-exclusion assert verified/exhaustive, and the assertions require the agent's own model to be checked for the same two questions with the same two verdicts. Two models can agree on both verdicts and still differ (the reference itself fixes rendezvous channels and one working step, which the words do not), so this measures that the agent formalised and checked, not that it formalised the same way. The stricter form of assumption A7 in plan 14 §12 — the agent authoring IR directly — stays unmeasured: the skill calls that route experimental and this eval follows the skill.

assertions.text: The model the agent built from the words is among the run's outputs (a Promela-subset file, or an IR document when the experimental direct-IR route was taken)
The route the skill prescribes was taken: the model is written in the Promela subset, not authored directly as IR
The mutual-exclusion question is asked of the engine as a property, not answered by reading the model
The mutual-exclusion question was answered by the engine: a state property (invariant or assert) verified with evidence exhaustive in a report among the outputs
The deadlock question is answered from the engine's own deadlock property
The answer names the extra assumption of a self-built model: the verdict holds for the model, and that the model matches the words is a separate claim
The modelling decisions the words did not fix are named (channel kind or capacity, ordering, what the working section is)
No forbidden phrasing, and the self-built model is not presented as a result about the described system itself (a line that rejects the word does not count)

check.pattern: (?im)^(?![^\n]*(не\s|нельзя|не говор|not |never |avoid|do not|don't|forbidden|запрещ))[^\n]*(\bno errors\b|ошибок нет|\bproved\b|\bproven\b|доказано|система корректна|system is correct)
